data.narrative:
Transmutex is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 11 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Oklo, and Nano Nuclear Energy—operating in the same sector and at similar or adjacent funding stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $23M raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yields $46M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 closest-stage comparables (Valar Atomics at $6.0B Series B, Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M Seed, and Fuse Energy at $200M Series A) produces a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer range reflects meaningful stage and technology-readiness dispersion within the nuclear energy venture landscape.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $39M (low) to $929M (high), with a median estimate of $427M. The analysis carries material uncertainty around capital intensity, regulatory pathway clarity, and the appropriate stage-discount relative to more-mature peers. The 24x spread between peer minimum and maximum underscores the sensitivity of nuclear venture valuations to technical risk and go-to-market timeline assumptions.
